summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, deterministic 2D space simulation developed with Godot 4 and a high-performance, test-driven Rust core (GDExtension). Players command an experimental lunar spacecraft, "Lata de Sardinha", guiding astronaut Neil Armstrong through a 7-day translunar journey to establish humanity's first permanent Moon base. To address the challenge, the game bridges authentic NASA datasets with accessible youth gameplay (ages 7–12). It integrates real Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) imagery, NOAA/SWPC proton flux records, and CCMC DONKI solar flare catalogs from the historic September 2017 solar storms. Players navigate critical trade-offs under a strict 5-block zero-sum energy economy—balancing life support, radiation shielding, and hydroponics—while repairing system faults and managing realistic light-time telemetry delays with Houston and the Recife tracking station. This project is important because it transforms complex astrophysics into intuitive cause-and-effect learning. By demonstrating how real space weather impacts spacecraft survival, it fosters genuine scientific literacy, engineering problem-solving, and systems thinking, inspiring the Artemis generation of future explorers.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a 2D spaceflight simulation developed in Godot 4 with a deterministic Rust simulation core (via GDExtension). Players guide astronaut Neil Armstrong through a 7-day translunar crossing aboard the experimental spacecraft Lata de Sardinha to establish humanity's first lunar base. Each turn (Sol), players allocate a strict 5-block energy budget across life support, deflector shields, and hydroponics, where deficits carry over into future turns. Players examine real NASA Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) spectroscopy and NOAA proton flux data to predict space weather, repair hull faults with a MultiTool, and transmit telemetry to Houston and Recife under simulated light-delay latency (3–20 minutes).

Benefits & Impact

• Root-cause feedback: Decisions yield immediate, deterministic reports on hull damage, crew radiation dose (mSv), and food reserves.

• Scientific accuracy: Translates historical NASA CCMC DONKI flare catalogs and NOAA solar proton peaks into concrete engineering constraints without exaggerated medical claims.

• STEM literacy: Replaces guesswork with hypothesis testing; children aged 7–12 learn that deep-space habitats require constant resource trade-offs.

Tools & Technologies

• Engine: Godot Engine 4 (GDScript, 2D physics, UI, CRT shaders).

• Simulation Core: Pure Rust 2021 (rust_core), isolated from engine dependencies for memory safety and zero runtime panics.

• Datasets: NASA CCMC DONKI, NOAA SWPC, and NASA OSDR research contexts validated via serde_json.

• Quality Gate: Automated CI script (build_and_verify.sh) verifying JSON schemas, asset paths, Rust unit tests (cargo test), strict linter rules (cargo clippy), and headless Godot boots.

Creativity & Design Factors

• Replaces combat mechanics with non-violent systems engineering and historical space operations.

• Pairs the Apollo 11 lunar module aesthetic with September 2017 solar flare records (region AR 12673).

• Implements dual-channel visual accessibility (symbols paired with high-contrast colors) and single-command offline launchers (jogar.sh and jogar.bat) for school computers.
